title: Madd silah and madd 'iwad: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
source: Written for quran/y9 lesson 3 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd silah and madd 'iwad rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 3. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: No silah
points: Letter before the haa is sakin: فِيهِ هُدًى
Next letter is sakin: لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ
Stopping on the haa: ذَكَرَهُۥ at a stop (74:55)

panels.title: Madd 'iwad
points: The tanween becomes a long aa, 2 counts
Not on taa marbutah (ـةً stops as haa)

head: Not this
This
rows: Stop as 'waheedaa': the tanween becomes a 2-count alif

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
the madd on the pronoun haa between two vowels
the alif replacing tanween fathah at a stop
a pronoun, here the haa meaning him or his

questions.q: Read 74:11 to 14 stopping at each ayah end; name the silah and 'iwad.
questions.a: Silah sughra: لَهُۥ مَالًۭا (74:12), لَهُۥ تَمْهِيدًۭا (74:14); 'iwad at the stops: وَحِيدَا, مَّمْدُودَا, شُهُودَا, تَمْهِيدَا.

questions.q: Silah and 'iwad audit (pupil PDF): mark them in 74:11 to 18 and 74:54 to 56. Today's rota group recites 74:38 to 56.
questions.a: Silah sughra: 74:12, 74:14, 74:16 إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ, 74:17 سَأُرْهِقُهُۥ صَعُودًا, 74:18 إِنَّهُۥ فَكَّرَ, 74:54 إِنَّهُۥ تَذْكِرَةٌ; 'iwad at stops: 74:11 to 14, 74:17; 74:55 ذَكَرَهُۥ at a stop: no silah.

questions.q: Extend: find a silah kubra in Al-Humazah.
Stretch: why do we stop on رَهِينَةٌ (74:38) as 'raheenah', not with an alif?
questions.a: It ends in taa marbutah: at a stop it becomes haa sakinah; 'iwad is only for tanween fathah on other letters.
A) lahoo: silah sughra, 2 counts. Between two vowelled letters, and the next letter is not hamza: sughra, 2 counts.

questions.q: Think again: Why do we read «لَهُۥ» as 'lahoo' but «لَهُ ٱلْ...» as 'lahul'?
questions.a: Silah only happens when the haa is between two vowelled letters; before a sukoon (or hamzat al-wasl) it is short.
